source: There's still time to save her, perhaps.
If I don't intervene, I know Father will be killed.
That means Hamlet will likely be sent to England, unless further circumstances deem otherwise.
If I can find a way to keep Rosencrantz and Guildenstern alive until the England-bound ship returns to harbor...
Maybe there's a way.
I'll need to get onto the ship first.
Who would have the authority to allow me on board, though?
I already know the King has the power to grant me access.
There's another option, too. If I can save Father's life-- perhaps I can keep them both safe from further harm.
I'll have to see what the next few days become.
By now, without my intervention, I know Father cannot be saved.
Oh, nothing. Rosie and I are leaving the castle, is all.
We have found Elsinore a most chilly welcome.
Totally unsatisfying.
Patently without class, poise, or even good wine.
Which would be all right, if the people were attractive...
But they aren't.
Well, except for you. And, I suppose, Hamlet. And... Horatio?
Certainly Horatio is a handsome man.
Yes, yes, we've debated this. Bernardo looks wonderful in everything. But I'm confident neither of them like women.
Lady Brit...?
With that attitude? Eugh.
Hmm. Yes. 'Eugh' indeed.
What she means to say is, we'll be departing shortly, forevermore.
And we wanted to bid you farewell.
Our everlasting thanks for saving us on the ship back there.
We'd most certainly have gone to a watery grave otherwise!
So, farewell, dearest Ophelia, you sweet angel of social manipulation.
Happiest of trails to you!
That is, unless...
...you wanted to come with us.
Oh, what a fascinating idea! You see, Guilda's taken quite the shine to you.
You're already color-complementary to the two of us, as trios go!
I'd love to. Let me gather my things and I'll come with you.
Let's be off, then, shall we?
W-well, I was in the middle of something rather important.
More important than us? Unlikely.
Come, now. Put that aside and live a little.
Back on the ship... you told me that time is repeating for you.
Back by the pond... you told me that time is repeating for you.
So simply come back and try it all again, why don't you?
You've got forever, after all. But this is our only lifetime!
Leave with Rosencrantz and Guildenstern?

source: (...She has a point.)
All of this—everything—has been so dire.
Maybe it's time I relaxed a moment.
That's the spirit!
(I could leave with them forever, now that I have the book.)
(Is this a life I could be happy with?)
We spent a long night cavorting and drinking at the pub in town. By the time the invasion inevitably swept through, we were all too inebriated to care.

source: I... can't.
Thank you for the invitation, but... I think I need to stay here, in Elsinore.
I'm sorry, Guildenstern.
Ah, well... your loss. I hope you have a splended life amongst the dour and dismal, my lady.
Come on, Guilda.
Goodbye, Ophelia.
(Perhaps in another life.)
How is her condition today?
I dunnah! Not improved, certainly. Still three kinds o' loony.
Ah, Ophelia...
Ophelia. Do you know us?
Of course. Perdita. You are lovelier than I ever thought possible.
And there's Florizel, the gallant prince, come to you at last.
Everything is lovely in the springtime.
Imagine me, gentle spectators, that I now may be in fair Bohemia!
The hills dotted with sheep, the trees all abloom... yes.
It shall stay so forever.
She's not comin' back, is she?
Not from this.
The Ophelia we knew is dead.
But she looks—happy. Peaceful. She's not in any pain.
Thank God for that. We've all suffered enough. Her, especially.
I wonder what her fantasy must be like. I wonder what she's seeing in there.
I just wish I could see that, at least.
I lie in an endless summer.

source: All right. Prepare yerselves for Irma house rules, peasants! No complaining, no shortchanging!
An' I'll watch the pot, of course.
And what's to stop you from sneaking off with the coin?
The fact that I'm a man of my damn honor, that's what!
Is the 'honor' part what makes your fingers so sticky?
Enough racket. Do you want Bernardo to hear you shouting and come running? No. I shall deal.
Tonight we play primero. I tire of Ruff and Honors. We play it far too often.
How abou' a little wine while you play, gents?
We... we're not supposed to...
The last time we drank before our shift, I ended up under the table, and Bernardo caught me and made me run thirty laps.
And I ended up in the bushes, and he made me clean all of his clothing by hand... even his undergarments!
Enough ninnyin' about. Let's play! You. Drink!
I've seen quite enough.
How long's she been hidin' in—I mean—ergh—m'lady!
We weren't doin' no harm!
Mmm. This looks awfully covert for a group who are operating above board.
Just give it to 'er! Whatever she needs. I can't run laps again like last time... my legs won' last another mile like that!
I'll meet an early grave if I, too, must run laps again. That bastard...
M-my lady, if you keep this quiet, I swear, I'll go against your father's orders! I'll let you into Castle Town!
Just meet me at the gates. Any time, my lady, I promise it!
Fascinating. Enjoy the rest of your card game, then.
My silence has a price, you know.
She's ruthless. What'd I tell you, Marcellus?
Just like her mother.
A-aye! Terrifyin'!
Just please don't tell Bernardo! I can't run laps again like last time... my legs won' last another mile like that!
Cygnus, I'll see you at the castle gates.
G-guard captain!
If you have time to gamble, surely you have time to train harder. Need I remind you all we are at war?
If you'd like me not to confiscate those, I suggest you spend less time mired in vice like a two-copper tavern wench and more time serving your ladyship. Now—go.
Honestly. I'm too lax on them...
Was I too hard on them? Are they acting out in spite?
I gave them everything! They just don't appreciate me.
(A gambling ring? So that's what the guards get up to in the evenings.)
(I doubt Bernardo would approve of this.)
Now is as good of a time as any to bring these supplies to Horatio.
I've collected what you asked for. Can you make the supplies you said you would?
Horatio, do you think if I gave you some supplies, you could produce some tools with which to make art?
Certainly. But I'd need some--
--Eggs, charcoal, and linen.
That's both eerie and unnerving.
So you'll do it? They're for Lady Brit.
Ah, of course!
Give me just a moment.
What are you two idiots doing? I have a permanent reservation on loitering here. Alone.
Actually, Brit, we brought you a gift.
I know you weren't able to find painting supplies here—so I've created some, with Horatio's help.
Now you can paint and draw again.
(...She still doesn't trust me. I wonder if there's something more I can do. Perhaps someone close to her knows.)
Might as well bring Brit these letters now.
Brit, I have something for you.
What are these?
Is this... are these... real?
They're from my mother.
Some of these are... months old. Where did you find them?
They were hidden inside the well on the grounds. I believe they were hidden there from you.
I see. Gertrude hid these from me.
And I thought I was the cruelest bitch I knew. Evidently not.
Mother wrote me every day, and she hid them from me. She lied to me.
Only because she thought she was keeping you happier by denying them to you.
Happy? The first month I came here, I wept every night, alone and afraid. How is that happy?
I heard nothing from my mother and thought she had abandoned me, forgotten me completely. Now I learn it was all a lie?
What kind of—she just—ugh. I hate Gertrude.
What kind of--she just--ugh. I wish I could... speak to her about this. To ask her why. But I can't even do that, can I?
Why won't you leave me alone? Why did you keep doing these things for me?
Why did you do this?
I want to be kind to you, Brit. I've been needlessly mean.
We don't have to be at odds.
I don't buy it. Get thee gone, you sniveling suck-up.
(...She still doesn't trust me. I wonder if there's something more I can do. Maybe I could find someone to help me.)
I told you to leave me alone.
What is wrong with you? You're like the thing that won't die. You keep coming back again and again.
I just—want to be—alone.
I know about Fortinbras. About your mission.
Yes, we went over this already. Though you still haven't elaborated how you know so much.
That doesn't matter now. I'm not here to have you locked up. I want to help you, Brit.
To the greatest extent that you'll let me. You can trust me.
W-what mission?
You don't have to act surprised. I'm not here to have you locked up. I want to help you, Brit.
Not here. Somewhere private. Come with me.
Claudius was supposed to die.
That's what I came to Elsinore to ensure.
Because my father thought, if Claudius were dead--
All this would be over. The war would end. Prince Fortinbras and my father would be appeased. And I could go home again.
As with many noble families, our roots run strong in Denmark. But Father believes Fortinbras will be a more sympathetic ruler.
Claudius has ignored most of the nobility's requests, even after I was placed here at court. Now my father and the other nobles want him gone.
The longer I go without succeeding, the more I just want to put down my head and sleep for a long time. Maybe forever.
But Fortinbras was placed under arrest. He's in the dungeon this very moment. What does it matter?
As if a prison can hold a man like that. He may be in prison now, but don't think for a moment he'll stay there.
His associates are almost certainly watching, just waiting to make their move and spring him free.
Hrm. Fortinbras's invasion... we spoke of it earlier. Do you remember?
What of it?
On the subject of domestic matters, I know Lord Fortinbras is going to invade Denmark soon.
I'm not certain how you learned that, but what difference does it make?
As I said before: leave me alone. We cannot be friends. And there can be no trust between us until this matter is resolved.
